OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH. 493

confession of the Lord and the one God; for this joins minds to Heaven and creates a distance from the East, upon which the Lord is.

829. Since religion resides in the highest parts of a human being, and from these highest parts his lower parts live and shine, and because Muhammad is involved in their minds together with their religion, some Muhammad is always placed in their view. In order that they may turn their faces toward the East, upon which the Lord is, he is placed below the Christian center <note>Latin: *Meditullium*</note>. It is not the Muhammad himself who wrote the <term>Alcoran</term> <gloss>Koran</gloss>, but another who performs his duty; nor is it always the same one, but he is changed. Once it was a man from Saxony who, having been captured by the Algerians, became a Muhammadan. Because he had also been a Christian, he was induced several times to speak to them about the Lord, that He was not the son of Joseph but the Son of God Himself. Other Muhammads have succeeded this one. In the place where that representative Muhammad has his seat, a fire like a torch appears so that he may be known; but that fire is not visible to others than Muhammadans.

830. The Muhammad himself who wrote the <term>Alcoran</term> does not come into view today. I was told that in earlier times he presided over them, but because he wished to rule over all matters of their religion as God, he was cast out from his seat, which he had held under the Roman Catholics, and was lowered to the right side near the south. Once, a certain society of Muhammadans was incited by malicious persons to acknowledge Muhammad as God. In order that the sedition might be quieted, Muhammad was brought up from the lower earth and shown, and at that time he was seen by me as well. He appeared like those corporeal spirits who have no interior perception, with a face tending toward black, and I heard him speak these words, "I am your Muhammad," and soon he seemed to sink down.

831. Muhammadans are hostile to Christians primarily because of the faith of three Divine Persons and the resulting worship of three Gods—as many creators—and furthermore, toward the Roman Catholics, because of their genuflections before images. Therefore they call the latter idolaters and the former fanatics, saying that they make a three-headed God, and that they say "one" while muttering "three," and consequently that they divide Omnipotence, and out of one and of the One they make three; and that they are like fauns with three horns, one for each god, and all three together for one; and that they pray in this way, chant in this way, and sound forth from the pulpits in this way.

832. Muhammadans, like all nations that acknowledge one God and love what is just and do what is good according to their religion, have their own Heaven, but it is outside the Christian Heaven. The Muhammadan Heaven is divided into two. In the lower one, they live honestly with several wives, but from there, no others are raised into the higher Heaven except those who renounce their concubines and acknowledge the Lord our Savior, and at the same time, His dominion over Heaven and Hell. I heard that it is impossible for them to think that God the Father and our Lord are one, but that it is possible for them to believe that He rules over the Heavens and Hells because He is the Son of God the Father. This faith is among them, through which ascent into the higher Heaven is granted to them by the Lord.

833. The fact that the Muhammadan religion has been received by more kingdoms than the Christian religion can be a scandal to those who think about Divine Providence and at the same time believe that no one can be saved except one who is born a Christian. But the Muhammadan religion is not a scandal to those who believe that all things are of Divine Providence. These inquire where it is, and they also find it. It lies in this: that the Muhammadan religion acknowledges the Lord as the Greatest Prophet, the wisest of all, and also as the Son of God. But because they have made the <term>Alcoran</term> the book of their religion, and consequently Muhammad, who wrote it, has taken hold of their thoughts, and they pay him some worship, they therefore think little of our Lord. So that it may be fully known that that religion was raised up by the Divine Providence of the Lord to destroy the idolatries of many nations, it will be told in some order, but first concerning the origin of idolatries. Before that religion, there was idolatrous worship—

<summary>Swedenborg describes the nature of the Muhammadan afterlife, the representation of Muhammad among them, and how their religion serves a providential purpose in curbing idolatry while acknowledging the Lord.</summary>
<keywords>Muhammad, Alcoran, Divine Providence, afterlife, idolatry, Christian faith, Heaven, religion</keywords>

For I have already seen the kingdoms which are an allusion to the seven <note>alternative: or "four", considering the context of the four chariots</note> kingdoms. And likewise, "what are these" <note>original: "מה אלה"</note> pertains to the matter of my life within them.

The angel answered and said to me: These are the four spirits of the heavens, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one in which are the black horses goes out to the land of the north; and the white ones went out after them; and the dappled ones went out to the land of the south. And the strong ones went out and sought to go, to walk about the earth; and he said: "Go, walk about the earth." And they walked about the earth. Then he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying: "Behold, those who go out to the land of the north have set my spirit at rest in the land of the north."

**And he answered.** "These are the four spirits." This is like "to the four spirits." And similarly, "and he came Jerusalem" <note>original: "ויבא ירושלם"</note> is like "to Jerusalem." Another explanation: "to the four" <note>clarification: explaining the prepositional use</note>, like "son of Shahor" is like "to the son of Shahor," and those similar to it. To the four divisions of the four chariots, and they go out to the four spirits <note>clarification: directions</note> of the heavens. All this is to give authority to the four kingdoms to rule in the four directions, each one in its time. All this is in the whole world, which is the meaning of strength. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth" <note>original: "מהתיצב על אדון כל הארץ"</note>. This means by the mission of God who gave them dominion over this. Just as it says: "And the sons of God came to stand before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin>

**In which.** "The black." And he did not mention the first <note>clarification: the first chariot/horses</note> because the time of the Babylonian kingdom had already passed. And the kingdom of Media and Persia went out first to the land of the north, for they were there to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. "And the white ones," which are the kingdom of Greece, "went out after them" because that kingdom was established <note>alternative: or "cleared"</note>. For Alexander of Macedon <note>term</note> <gloss>Alexander the Great</gloss>, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingship from him and reigned; and afterward his successors <note>unclear>קוז וקכחיס</note> reigned after him in the whole world.

**And the dappled ones went out to the land of the south.** For they were the portion of <unclear>קדוס</unclear> because Rome is <unclear>שנונית</unclear>. And <term>Augustus</term> <gloss>Octavian</gloss> Caesar, who reigned over Rome, began to fight against the kingdom of Greece; and at the beginning of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is southern. And in all the lands, the sons of Greece were then ruling. And <term>Augustus</term> Caesar prevailed over them and transferred the kingship from the sons of Greece and returned it to the Romans.

**And the strong ones.** They are an allusion to the kingdom of Ishmael <note>context: traditional rabbinic identification for the Islamic Caliphate/Arabs</note> who exerted themselves <note>clarification: or "strengthened themselves"</note> on their own to seek kingship, to find a place to dwell, for there was a spirit granted to them. And this is what it says: "And they sought to go, to walk about the earth."

**And he said.** That is to say, he gave them permission to walk about and to conquer lands.

**And he cried out.** That is to say, he called to me with a great voice and said to me: **"Behold, those who go out to the land of the north have set my spirit at rest in the land of the north."** That is to say, the portion of the black ones who went out to Babylon to destroy it.

<summary>A commentary on Zechariah 6 explaining the vision of the four chariots and horses as symbols for historical empires: Media-Persia, Greece, Rome, and the Arabs.</summary>
<keywords>Zechariah, four spirits, Babylon, Media, Persia, Greece, Rome, Ishmael, Alexander the Great, Augustus Caesar</keywords>

you encounter a gathering. Furthermore (which is more wonderful), the stars called by astronomers until this day *Nebulosae* <gloss>nebulae</gloss> are groups of stars arranged in a wonderful way. From the mixture of their rays, while each one escapes the sharpness of the eyes due to its smallness or its extreme distance from us, that brightness arises which, until now, has been believed to be a denser part of the heavens capable of reflecting the rays of the stars or the Sun. We have observed some of them; and we have decided to subjoin the asterisms <gloss>constellations/star groups</gloss> of two.

In the first, you have the *Nebulosa* <gloss>nebula</gloss> called of the Head of Orion, in which we counted twenty-one stars.

The second contains the *Nebulosa* <gloss>nebula</gloss> named Praesepe <gloss>Manger/Beehive Cluster</gloss>, which is not merely one star, but a mass of more than forty stars. Besides the Aselli <gloss>Donkeys</gloss>, we have noted thirty-six arranged in the following order.

For he has a portion in the holy people, more so than all, in the faith <note>clarification: the power of faith</note> to receive guests and to rejoice in this world and the world to come. A person must cause the poor to rejoice, because the portion of those guests <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>mystical celestial guests</gloss> who are invited belongs to the poor. One who sits in the wholeness of faith and invites these exalted guests, the guests of faith, but does not give them their portion <note>clarification: by failing to feed the poor</note>, they all stand over him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of one who has an evil eye...** <note>original: "אל תלחם את לחם רע עין וגו'" (Proverbs 23:6)</note>

It turns out that the table he prepared is his own and not the Holy One’s, blessed be He. Concerning him it is written:
> **I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festivals...** <note>original: "וזרתי פרש על פניכם וגו' פרש חגיכם וגו'" (Malachi 2:3)</note>

Woe to that person at the time when those guests of faith rise from the table. Rabbi Abba said: All the days of Abraham, he would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and receive them at his table. Now that people invite him <note>context: as a mystical guest during the festival of Sukkot</note> and all the righteous ones and King David, but do not give them their portion, it is the hardest thing of all, and it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men...** <note>original: "סורו נא מעל אהלי האנשים הרשעים האלה" (Numbers 16:26)</note>

And they all ascend and say: <term>Yitzhak</term> <gloss>Isaac</gloss> says:
> **But the belly of the wicked shall want.** <note>original: "ובטן רשעים תחסר" (Proverbs 13:25)</note>

<term>Ya'akov</term> <gloss>Jacob</gloss> says:
> **The morsel you have eaten, you shall vomit up.** <note>original: "פתך אכלת תקיאנה" (Proverbs 23:8)</note>

And all the other righteous ones say:
> **For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that there is no place clean.** <note>original: "כי כל שלחנות מלאו קיא צואה בלי מקום" (Isaiah 28:8)</note>

<term>David Malka</term> <gloss>King David</gloss> spoke of the laws of oppression, for David suffered and made himself a guest, yet the man did not desire him, did not invite him, and did not give him his portion. And since the crown and the right hand of King David sustain the world, that man who robs him causes more damage than any other. Rabbi Elazar said: A person is exempt from acts of kindness <term>hasiduta</term> <gloss>piety/loving-kindness</gloss> except according to what they are able, as it is written "according to the gift of his hand." First, one should satisfy and gladden themselves, and what remains should be given to the poor; this is the very spirit of the guests. The Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with them and calls out a blessing:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord...** <note>original: "אז תתענג על יי' וגו'" (Isaiah 58:14)</note>

And Isaac calls out over him:
> **No weapon formed against you shall prosper.** <note>original: "כל כלי יוצר עליך לא יצלח" (Isaiah 54:17)</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: King David said this because all the armaments of the King and the battles of the King are entrusted into the hands of David. Happy is the one who rejoices in his portion. Jacob said of him: "Then your light shall break forth as the morning." The other righteous ones said: "And the Lord shall guide you continually, and satisfy your soul." King David said: "No weapon formed against you shall prosper," for he is appointed over all types of armaments. This is the portion of a person who merits all these merits. Regarding the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come, it is written:
> **And your people shall all be righteous...** <note>original: "ועמך כלם צדיקים וגו'" (Isaiah 60:21)</note>

---

### The Faithful Shepherd <note>original: "רעיא מהימנא" (Ra'aya Meheimna)</note>

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day...** <- <note>original: "ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון וגו'" (Leviticus 23:40)</note>

This **commandment** <term>pikuda</term> is to take the <term>lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> as is proper during these days. This contains a secret: just as the Holy One, blessed be He, took Israel at this time of judgment, so too must they seek the Holy One as their portion and take hold of Him. The first of these is the palm branch, which represents the secret of the image of Adam <note>clarification: the primordial man</note>.

The Holy One, blessed be He, created Adam in His image, as it is written: "And God created man in His own image." Furthermore, he is called "Elohim" <note>clarification: a title of authority/divinity</note> at the time when truth and radiance emerge in the world. It is written: "You shall not revile God <term>Elohim</term>," referring to his greatness, for it is written: "And God created 

---

man in His image." And it has been well established that it is written: **"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness,"** which was said at the time of the union <note>clarification: the mystical union of divine attributes</note>. Such is the intention of both, "image" <term>tselem</term> and "likeness" <term>demut</term>, representing the male and female that emerged together. "And God created man in His own image." We find that when the King ascends, it occurs at the time of the union.

<summary>This page discusses the mystical significance of the 'Ushpizin' (celestial guests) during Sukkot, emphasizing that failing to feed the poor alienates these divine visitors. It also begins a discourse from the 'Faithful Shepherd' on the commandment of the Lulav and the creation of man in the divine image.</summary>

<keywords>Ushpizin, Sukkot, charity, poor, King David, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Lulav, Divine Image, Tselem, Demut, Ra'aya Meheimna</keywords>

<meta>The text continues the narrative of a protagonist who has been deceived by the protagonist Abu Zayd al-Saruji, now seeking redress from a judge.</meta>

he had none other than him. So I did for the judge, or do you know his father? May God <note>clarification: bless</note> his latter state. He said: And am I ignorant of Abu Zayd, whose wound was caused by an oppressor <note>original: "جَبَّارٌ"</note>, and who has, before every judge, news and reports? At that moment I shaved <note>clarification: my head in grief or shame</note> and woke up, but only when the time had passed. I became certain that for every <unclear>his all</unclear> his evil was a ruse and the theme of a poem. Then what I encountered made my gaze sink, and I swore that I would not deal with the likes of those two as long as I remain. Then I did cease to sigh over the best of my bargain and the <unclear>clarity</unclear> among my companions. The judge said to me when he saw what had transpired, and a free man’s clarity became evident: O you, what has gone from your wealth is not lost if it has warned you, nor has he committed a crime against you who has awakened you. So take heed from what has come to you, and let your companions <note>clarification: be a lesson regarding</note> what befell you. Remember forever what overcame you, so that for the sake of the memory you may expel your dirhams <note>gloss: silver coins</note> and wear out <note>clarification: the memory of loss</note>. He who is afflicted and endures is worn out, and the lesson was revealed to him, so he took heed. So I bid him farewell, while shame and sadness did not ask for a path <note>clarification: to me, as they were already present</note>, the tail of fraud and deception <note>original: "الْغَبْنِ وَالْغَبْنِ"</note> trailing behind. I intended to confront Abu Zayd with the news directly.

<meta>This page contains the Persian text of Rūmī's Masnavī with an Ottoman Turkish interlinear translation and commentary in the columns. The passage focuses on the tripartite nature of creation as explained in a prophetic tradition.</meta>

| | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Like a stubborn donkey with its feet tied, | He tied both its feet and on the head, | Like a blindfolded donkey, it pulled its head and in, |
| Then the donkey says one binding is enough for me, | That very action is the deed of that vile one, | Verily, one binding is enough for a donkey in weeping, |

### Explanation of that Hadith of Mustafa <note>context: The Prophet Muhammad</note>, peace be upon him: "Indeed, God Almighty created the angels and placed intellect in them; He created the beasts and placed desire in them; and He created the children of Adam and placed both intellect and desire in them. He whose intellect overcomes his desire is higher than the angels, and he whose desire overcomes his intellect is lower than the beasts." The Messenger of God spoke the truth.

<column-break/>

God the Glorious created the world's creatures in three ways. One group is predominantly intellect, knowledge, and generosity; that is the angel, who knows nothing but prostration. There is no greed or passion in their element; they are absolute light, living by the love of God. Another group is void of knowledge, like animals finding beauty in fodder. They think of nothing but the stable and feed; out of wretchedness they are wise, and void of honor. This third kind is the child of Adam and human; half of him is inclined toward the higher realm, while the other half—the donkey—is inclined toward the lower. These two <note>clarification: the angels and the beasts</note> groups are at rest from war and strife, but humans are divided into three communities through trial. One group has become absolutely submerged, joined with the angels like Jesus. They are released from anger, passion, and idle talk; they have the form of a man but the meaning of Gabriel. They are freed from spiritual discipline, asceticism, and struggle. The other group has joined with the beasts; they have become pure anger and absolute desire. The house of the body was narrow and that Gabriel-like quality in them was lost. He made them dead, like a person who is soulless, for the soul that does have the Beloved is base. Such a one lives a life lower than the animals. The deception and trickery he knows how to weave, the weaving of gold-embroidered robes, the finding of pearls in the depths of the sea, along with astronomy, medicine, and philosophy—these have no path to the seventh heaven. All of this relates to the stable <note>clarification: the material world</note>, for this science is the pillar of the beast's life. They gave these things names like "secrets of the universe," but the goal is merely the preservation of the animal for a few days.

<column-break/>

<note>original: "ایتد اوچ قسم اوزره مخلوقی بدید" (etdi üç kısm üzere mahlûku bedîd)</note>
<margin>
He made the creatures visible in three categories. Those who are angels prostrate. They became the manifestation of the love of God. Some became mixed with animality. They are heedless, wretched, and without honor. Others became prepared for both good and evil. The other half, like an angel, is noble-born. Human nature is moved by these two opposites. Man took the form of three communities. Those of the angelic rank truly reach the station of angels. They are released from anger, passion, and gossip. Do not think of them as merely human-born. The last group is of animal character, pure anger and absolute desire. The house of the body is narrow and that high quality is ruined. The soul that is without the Beloved becomes abased. This speech is the word of Truth; let it adorn your hand. He performs every precise task in the world, yet no animal can perform such deeds. He draws jewels from the depths of the sea. He is learned in philosophy, medicine, and astronomy. But he has no passage to the seventh heaven. He pays mind only to the ox and the donkey. He gave the name "mysteries" to those follies.
</margin>

<note>image: A decorative border surrounding the text columns.</note>

<summary>This page explains a Prophetic tradition regarding the three types of beings: angels (intellect), animals (desire), and humans (a struggle between both). It critiques worldly sciences like medicine and philosophy as being "animal sciences" if they only serve physical preservation rather than spiritual ascent.</summary>
<keywords>intellect, desire, angels, beasts, humanity, Jesus, Gabriel, worldly science, spiritual struggle, Nafs</keywords>
